options: A list of promised members with no implementation (bar optional defaults)
explanation: An interface is a contract: what implementers must provide, nothing about how. No fields, no constructors.

stem: class Robot : IMovable, ISpeaker - is this allowed?
options: Yes - a class may implement any number of interfaces
explanation: One base class, unlimited interfaces - C#'s answer to multiple inheritance without its ambiguity.

stem: SaveGame(IStorage storage) instead of SaveGame(FileStorage storage) buys you what?
options: Any implementation - memory, file, cloud, test fake - can be swapped in without changing SaveGame
explanation: Program to the interface, not the implementation. It is the D of SOLID and the single habit that makes code testable.

stem: students.Sort() works on your Student class if it implements:
explanation: CompareTo teaches the framework your ordering: negative = I come first, 0 = equal, positive = later. Sort calls it.

stem: You want to share FIELDS and some implemented code among related classes. Which fits?
explanation: Interfaces cannot hold state. An abstract class can carry fields, constructors and shared code - at the cost of using the class's single inheritance slot.

stem: Rule of thumb: use an interface for a ____ .
explanation: Interfaces name what something CAN DO. Unrelated types - a Robot and a Duck - can share a capability with no shared ancestry.

stem: An interface method WITH a body (C# 8 default implementation) is reachable how?
explanation: Defaults live on the interface, not the class - a surprise worth knowing. Their main use is evolving a published interface without breaking implementers.

stem: string IFlyer.Fly() => ...;  (no access modifier, interface-qualified name) makes Fly:
options: Reachable ONLY through an IFlyer reference
explanation: Explicit implementation hides the member from the class's own surface - used for name clashes between interfaces, or to keep the contract off the main API.

stem: Implementing IEnumerable<T> on your class gives it:
options: foreach support AND all of LINQ
explanation: foreach and every LINQ operator are written against IEnumerable<T> - one GetEnumerator and your Playlist joins the ecosystem (3.5).

stem: Why does writing 'public' on an interface member declaration cause an error in classic style?
options: Interface members are public BY DEFINITION - the modifier is redundant/disallowed
explanation: A contract that nobody could see would be pointless - interface members are inherently public, so the modifier is not written.
